name: Expeditors
description: Expeditors is an asset-light global freight forwarder and customs broker: it buys cargo space from airlines and ocean carriers and resells it to shippers, and files customs paperwork and arranges destination delivery. It owns no aircraft, has 172 district offices and about 20,000 employees. Its gross revenue swings with freight rates, so net revenue (revenue less directly related transport cost) is the better measure: about $1.0B air, $0.8B ocean and $1.9B customs brokerage and other in 2025. Operating income was $1,053M (9.5% of gross revenue) in 2025.

businessLines.name: Airfreight services
businessLines.how: Buys air cargo capacity in bulk and resells it per shipment (consolidation), or forwards individual shipments as agent; revenue = tonnage x sell rate, margin is the buy/sell spread.

businessLines.name: Ocean freight and ocean services
businessLines.how: Acts as non-vessel-operating carrier: buys container space from shipping lines and resells it; also direct forwarding and order management.

businessLines.name: Customs brokerage and other services
businessLines.how: Fees per customs entry and for import services, road freight, warehousing and distribution; grew double digits as tariff complexity raised demand for brokerage.
